records.ieeg_reference: Locally referenced within each recording site, using either one of the eight microwires of the bundle or a dedicated lower-impedance reference wire of the bundle (Daume et al. 2024, Methods); the reference wire per channel is not given in the release.

SpikeRemovalAndDownsamplingByAuthors.Description: NWB description of the series: 'These are LFP recordings that have spike potentials removed and is downsampled to 400Hz'. Daume et al. (2024, Methods): spike waveforms removed by linear interpolation from -1 to 2 ms around each spike onset (on all wires of the bundle), then zero phase-lag low-pass at 175 Hz and downsampling to 400 Hz. The article then removes line noise (59.5-60.5 and 119.5-120.5 Hz band-stop) for its analysis; whether this band-stop is applied to the released series is not stated. None of this was applied by the BIDS conversion.

records.ieeg_reference: Locally referenced within each recording site, using either one of the eight microwires of the bundle or a dedicated lower-impedance reference wire of the bundle (Daume et al. 2024, Methods); the reference wire per channel is not given in the release.

SpikeRemovalAndDownsamplingByAuthors.Description: NWB description of the series: 'These are LFP recordings that have spike potentials removed and is downsampled to 400Hz'. Daume et al. (2024, Methods): spike waveforms removed by linear interpolation from -1 to 2 ms around each spike onset (on all wires of the bundle), then zero phase-lag low-pass at 175 Hz and downsampling to 400 Hz. The article then removes line noise (59.5-60.5 and 119.5-120.5 Hz band-stop) for its analysis; whether this band-stop is applied to the released series is not stated. None of this was applied by the BIDS conversion.

Broadband.Description: Broadband signal recorded between 0.1 and 8000 Hz at 32 kHz (ATLAS, Neuralynx; Cedars-Sinai and Toronto Western) or 30 kHz (Blackrock Neurotech; Johns Hopkins) (Daume et al. 2024, Methods).
